newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Major says no deal on Gibraltar.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Major says no deal on Gibraltar.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major said on Thursday that Britain was not prepared to accept a deal with Spain on the sovereignty of the British colony of Gibraltar.
Major, answering a question in parliament, said: "Britain stands by its commitment of the people of Gibraltar...
"We will not be entering into arrangements under which the people of Gibraltar would pass under the sovereignty of another state against their freely-expressed wishes."
Spain last week proposed sharing sovereignty over Gibraltar for the next 100 years and then handing control of the colony to Madrid, the Foreign Office said this week.
Spain's Foreign Minister Abel Matutes made the offer during a visit to Madrid of his British counterpart Malcolm Rifkind. Rifkind turned down the proposal.
Britain and Spain have wrangled over the sovereignty of the 5.8 square km (2.2 square miles) colony at the tip of the Iberian peninsula for many years.
Britain seized the colony from Spain in 1704. It was ceded by Spain in perpetuity under the 1713 Treaty of Utrecht.
Spain's insistence that it is disputed territory has soured relations between the two countries for decades.

In a 1967 referendum in Gibraltar, 99 percent of the people voted to remain British. Britain has insisted that the people of Gibraltar must be consulted on any change in the sovereignty of the colony.
